title: Agent borrowing costs are scheduled to move from a flat Base Rate to per-Agent risk-based pricing
content:
A.3.1.2.5.1 makes the flat borrow rate provisional: the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate "is equal to the Base Rate **unless** variable pricing has been activated," after which it "will vary by Prime Agent according to its Credit Rating." A.3.1.2.5.5 confirms the sequencing — differentiation waits on "the development of a Prime Agent Credit Rating System."

The Atlas is unusually specific about what would feed that rating: "the Encumbrance Ratio and the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry." That pairing is the interesting part. One input is financial (how much of the Agent's capacity is already committed); the other is *operational security history* — an Agent that has had smart-contract security incidents pays more to borrow.

Pricing security posture into cost of capital is a different lever from the usual ones. Rather than reviewing an Agent's code or revoking its access after an incident, Sky makes carelessness continuously expensive, so remediation has a measurable payback and the incentive persists between audits.

Until activation, all Prime Agents pay the same Base Rate regardless of risk — so during the interim, cross-subsidization of riskier Agents by safer ones is an accepted cost of not yet having the rating machinery.
description: Once a Prime Agent Credit Rating System exists, the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate varies by rating, computed from inputs including the Encumbrance Ratio and the Prime Spell Security Incident Registry.
